Main article: [Seven Years' War](/wiki/Seven_Years%27_War "Seven Years' War")

With the British victory in the Seven Years' War, France in 1763 ceded to Britain its claims of North American territories east of the [Mississippi River](/wiki/Mississippi_River "Mississippi River"). Spain, in turn, gained rights to the territories west of Mississippi, which then served as a border between Spain and Britain's territorial claims. French colonists settled [Illinois Country](/wiki/Illinois_Country "Illinois Country") after several generations of experience on North America, migrating over the Mississippi River to regions where Spain was not present and where they were able to leverage their earlier Louisiana French settlements around the [Gulf of Mexico](/wiki/Gulf_of_Mexico "Gulf of Mexico"). These early French settlers partnered with midwest indigenous tribes, and their mixed ancestry descendants later followed a westward expansion all the way to the [Pacific Ocean](/wiki/Pacific_Ocean "Pacific Ocean") on the present-day [U.S. West Coast](/wiki/U.S._West_Coast "U.S. West Coast").

After drafting him in the second round of the [2005 NFL draft](/wiki/2005_NFL_draft "2005 NFL draft"),[[3]](#cite_note-3) the Cardinals placed him as the starting running back on the depth chart, with the intention of having him share carries with [Marcel Shipp](/wiki/Marcel_Shipp "Marcel Shipp"). He started the first game against the [New York Giants](/wiki/New_York_Giants "New York Giants") gaining 5 yards on 8 carries (0.625 average). After this poor showing in his first game, he didn't play a snap the second game of the season against the [St. Louis Rams](/wiki/St._Louis_Rams "St. Louis Rams"). By the end of the season, he had played 15 games with 5 starts, gaining 370 yards on 112 carries (3.3 average) and 2 touchdowns. That following offseason the Cardinals signed [Edgerrin James](/wiki/Edgerrin_James "Edgerrin James").

The Cardinals' drafting of [Tim Hightower](/wiki/Tim_Hightower "Tim Hightower") in 2008 resulted in Arrington being shifted to third place on the depth chart at running back. He became the team's principal kick returner and in [Super Bowl XLIII](/wiki/Super_Bowl_XLIII "Super Bowl XLIII") caught 2 passes for 35 yards.

Arrington signed with the [Denver Broncos](/wiki/Denver_Broncos "Denver Broncos") on March 4, 2009. He was released on May 27, 2009, after failing his physical.[[4]](#cite_note-4) It was determined that Arrington would need season-ending microfracture surgery on his right knee,[[5]](#cite_note-5) following surgery to the same knee in February. He was re-signed on March 4, 2010.

Adams spent the winter of 1795–1796 in [London](/wiki/London "London"), where he met [Louisa Catherine Johnson](/wiki/Louisa_Adams "Louisa Adams"), the second daughter of American merchant Joshua Johnson. In April 1796, Louisa accepted Adams's proposal of marriage. Adams's parents disapproved of his decision to marry a woman who had grown up in England, but he informed his parents that he would not reconsider his decision.[[24]](#cite_note-25) Adams initially wanted to delay his wedding to Louisa until he returned to the United States, but they married in [All Hallows-by-the-Tower](/wiki/All_Hallows-by-the-Tower "All Hallows-by-the-Tower") on July 26, 1797.[[25]](#cite_note-26)[[b]](#cite_note-28) Shortly after the wedding, Joshua Johnson fled England to escape his creditors, and Adams did not receive the dowry that Johnson had promised him, much to the embarrassment of Louisa. Adams noted in his own diary that he had no regrets about his decision to marry Louisa.[[27]](#cite_note-29)

In 1796, Washington appointed Adams as the [U.S. minister to Portugal](/wiki/List_of_ambassadors_of_the_United_States_to_Portugal "List of ambassadors of the United States to Portugal").[[28]](#cite_note-30) Soon, however, John Adams defeated Jefferson in the [1796 presidential election](/wiki/1796_United_States_presidential_election "1796 United States presidential election"). The lower region of the valley receives less rainfall than the upper regions of the south; the lower boroughs of [Iztapalapa](/wiki/Iztapalapa "Iztapalapa"), [Iztacalco](/wiki/Iztacalco "Iztacalco"), [Venustiano Carranza](/wiki/Venustiano_Carranza,_D.F.
